title: Deep links - seven rows of ad-hoc URL-parameter handling across three bundles
why: Three bundles - `app.html`, `app-tenant.html` and `maya-os-site/index.html` - each handle their own overlapping set of query parameters, and the sets are not equal: the public-site bundle carries the whole `app.html` deep-link surface plus `?consent` (S-618), so it, not `app.html`, is the bundle that defines full parity. Two different mechanisms sit in this group. The producers: the calendar-setup redirect exists twice (`lgOpenAppCal`, `onbOpenApp`), each writing `me_booking_backend` / `me_booking_api_base` / `me_booking_tenant_slug` to localStorage before a full-page `location.replace`, and each pinning a different workspace (S-547). The consumers: `?booking_backend` / `?booking_api_base` / `?booking_tenant` are read again at component level with no gate - verified in all three bundles (S-613, S-616) - alongside the gated boot read that `app.html` and the site bundle also carry (S-616). A URL parameter naming which API origin the app talks to is an authority input arriving through presentation.
disappear: The per-bundle ad-hoc parsers, and with them the ungated component-level reads of `booking_backend` / `booking_api_base` / `booking_tenant`; all three copies must be hardened in one pass, because fixing two of three is cosmetic (S-613, S-616). The two divergent calendar-setup producers collapse into a single entry point (S-547). The second live copy of the `?promo=reset` affordance goes with it, so the public bypass of the user's "never show again" choice stops existing in both bundles rather than one (S-612). The ad-hoc nav parameters `?onboarded` / `?calendar_setup` / `?crm_connect` / `?cabinet` retire together with primary navigation in `app.html`, but only if the public-site copy retires in the same pass (S-617).
remain: ONE declared deep-link vocabulary resolving to declared capabilities - CRM connect, calendar setup, onboarding, consent, promo, tips, social link, booking backend selection - with backend selection decided by server-side authority rather than by a URL-named origin. Parity is proven against the site bundle's superset list, not against `app.html` (S-618). The `?consent` force-show stays reachable: it is the 152-FZ entry point `app.html` does not carry, and what happens to it must be a recorded decision, not a casualty of treating `app.html` as canonical (S-618). `onbOpenApp`'s clearing of `me_saas_workspace_v1:<ns>` and the login-time routing that steers calendar setup to 'panel' must survive the merge, or post-onboarding users land in the wrong workspace and first-run calendar onboarding silently stops opening (S-547, S-068). The site bundle's `?device_id` reader - the legacy VK callback shape, whose loss breaks any VK return that lands on that host - and the two divergent cabinet allow-lists are deliberate calls, not silent drops; the allow-lists reconcile three ways, not two (S-618, S-617).
risk: HIGH for the `booking_*` family. The exposure these rows prove is not a stranger guessing another salon's namespace - no row here names a crossed tenant boundary - it is that `?booking_api_base` names the API origin that authenticated traffic is sent to, which S-616 calls the "Bearer-to-attacker-host path"; the same ungated component-level read is verified in all three bundles, `app-tenant` among them, and that is the tenant-scoped bundle, the one most likely to be opened from a link sent to a salon owner (S-613). MEDIUM for the rest: a merge that treats `app.html` as canonical silently drops the 152-FZ consent force-show and the site bundle's `device_id` reader (S-618); `social_link_error` echoes attacker-authored copy (S-618); a careless producer merge lands post-onboarding users in the wrong workspace, and a chat-driven navigation that skips `location.replace` boots the consumer with no backend base (S-547); retiring nav deep links in `app.html` alone leaves them live on the public host (S-617). Nothing in these seven rows bears on attendance confirmation, STEP_UP_VERIFIED, Gate 10 or approval separation, so the frozen limitations are untouched here.
user_impact: Invisible for two of the seven rows, not five. Only S-613 and S-616 are backend-pinning plumbing (`?booking_backend` / `?booking_api_base` / `?booking_tenant` written into `me_booking_*` localStorage); every other row has a live external producer. First run is the loudest: after signup or login the app opens calendar setup via `?calendar_setup=1` (S-068, S-547), and the two producers pin different workspaces (`lgOpenAppCal` -> business/schedule vs `onbOpenApp` -> choose, which additionally clears `me_saas_workspace_v1:<ns>`), so a careless merge either stops opening calendar setup after onboarding or lands a just-onboarded owner in the wrong workspace; S-547 adds the failure mode this rebuild actually creates — a chat-driven in-app navigation replacing the full-page `location.replace` skips the `me_booking_*` write and the consumer boots with no backend base at all. S-618 is not plumbing: besides `?consent=1` it carries `?tips=<master>`, the post-visit tips push landing (maya-os-site L19115-19125), and `?device_id`, the VK OAuth return reader (L37654) — external producers (a push, an OAuth callback) that break silently if the merge treats app.html as canonical. S-617 is the staff-facing routing row, but the divergence is not between bundles: app.html and maya-os-site ship byte-identical `?cabinet` allow-lists — 8 values post-onboarding (app.html L6936, site L5656) and 11 values on the login route (app.html L38605, site L35673, the pair that adds `analytics`, `integrations`, `connect`). What decides whether those three stay reachable from a pasted link is reconciling the narrow list against the wide one, and that reconciliation has to be made in both copies. Nor is the `?promo` affordance the only deliberate loss: S-612's `?promo=1` forces the banner while `?promo=reset` deletes `promoNeverShow`/`promoShownOnce` outright — the "never show again" choice is erased, not overridden once — and the recommended booking-backend hardening additionally costs the app's own minted links, maya-site.html L245/L397 "Живое демо" and maya-admin.html L996/L1147 preview URLs, unless the successor keeps an allow-listed equivalent.
security_impact: An improvement in direction, but today's state is worse than described and the danger sits in a different bundle than the text says. In app.html and maya-os-site the boot reader is host-gated (the public domain refuses `?booking_backend`/`?booking_api_base` and regex-validates the slug — app.html L795, site L628) while a second, UNGATED component-level reader persists the same values into localStorage. `app-tenant.html` (S-613) has no gate at all: no `isLocalDev`/`isPrivateHost` branch, no slug regex, only the ungated read at L6851-6870 — so "the boot-level reader is already gated" is false for precisely the bundle a tenant link to a salon owner opens. The token claim also lands on the wrong bundle: in app-tenant the Bearer comes from `ensureLocalSession()` (L7036), which auto-mints a throwaway booking client (`booking-<ts>@maya.local` with a hardcoded password) and POSTs those credentials plus the returned token to `localSaasApiBase` — a credential leak and a fully attacker-fed booking UI, but not an owner's session. The owner-session leak is S-616: maya-os-site drives the real SaaS session through the same base, including `saasRawRefresh` POSTing the long-lived REFRESH token to `localSaasApiBase + '/auth/refresh'` (L10080) and a Bearer `/auth/logout` (L10150), so one crafted link leaks more than an access token. The improvement is real only if the fix lands in all three bundles in the same pass and is an allow-list rather than a delete: the app mints these URLs itself (maya-site "Живое демо" L245/L397, maya-admin preview L996/L1147), so a blanket refusal breaks the owner's live preview and the public demo. Two smaller items: `?consent=1`, the 152-FZ consent force-show, exists in the superset site bundle (L22036), so a merge treating app.html as canonical silently drops a consent-gate entry point along with the `?device_id` OAuth-return reader (S-618); and `social_link_error` is echoed verbatim as UI copy on a trusted profile screen (`socialMessage = linkError`, app.html L34741; site L31392) — attacker-authored text usable for phishing, not an authority bypass. Nothing here touches server-side role decisions, and no frozen limitation (fail-closed 13/21, STEP_UP unreachable, Gate 10 measured not enforced, approval role-gated rather than separation-of-duties, GAP-ATTENDANCE-CONFIRM open) is affected either way.
